clue.text: (& 25ac./21dn.) Say, for instance, you found a slasher movie gory, don't startle anybody

definitions.text: Say, for instance, you found a slasher movie gory, don't startle anybody

blocks.clueFragment: Say, for instance, you found a slasher movie gory
blocks.note: surface reading: a film-goer's verdict on a horror film
setter's reading: remarking that a slasher film is gory tells nobody anything new, and the gory film is literally bloody

explanation.surface: A cinema-goer complains about a gory slasher film while warning someone not to make others jump.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying a slasher movie is gory is a remark nobody needs telling; 'bleeding' is also a nod to the blood on screen. Bleeding is a mild British intensifier.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to voice something so plain that it surprises no one, exactly like calling a slasher film gory.

clue.text: How horrible to be besieged by crazy Tone's temper

indicators.note: something crazy is disordered, so the letters of the following name are jumbled
a besieged town is surrounded, so the exclamation sits inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled
an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled at a crazy man called Tone and his bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' looks like a noun meaning mood, but it is the verb, as in tempering steel.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper metal is to harden it, and to toughen is likewise to make stronger and more resistant.

clue.text: Object of spin: to elevate and refresh

definitions.note: TOP-UP is hyphenated as a noun; the verb is 'top up'

blocks.note: a spinning top is the toy you spin
to up something is to raise it

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor's aims: raise the profile and freshen the image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' suggests political media management, but the object spun is a child's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Topping up a drink refreshes it by filling the glass again.

clue.text: (& 6dn.) Nibble time, with sex mouthpiece

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
'it' is a coy word for sex
a horse's bit is the metal piece in its mouth

explanation.surface: A saucy picture of nibbling, timing and sex with something in the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouthpiece' sounds like a spokesperson or part of an instrument; it is the bit in a horse's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small tasty morsel, the kind of snack one would nibble.

clue.text: It's involved with Gnome feeling like a luvvie

indicators.note: things involved are tangled together, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden gnome somehow showing the feelings of a theatrical type.
explanation.walkthrough: A luvvie is British slang for a gushing, self-regarding actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Emoting is showing feelings in an exaggerated, theatrical way, just as a luvvie would.

clue.text: Toss, with tip of knob in cylinder

indicators.note: the tip of something is its very end, here the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: to bob is to toss or jerk up and down
the word's tip
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crude Private Eye image of tossing and a knob's tip in a tube.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is smutty slang; 'Toss' is just a bobbing movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobbin is the small spool or cylinder on which thread is wound.

clue.text: see 4dn.
Conservative 2/3 of Labour goes around without one

indicators.note: only two thirds of the word is used, so its opening third is dropped
turned around, the following word's letters are rearranged
without in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled word sits around the numeral

blocks.note: taken as written; its last four letters are kept
taken as written, then jumbled
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A jibe that a Labour party shorn of a third turns out conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' looks like a party label; it is the adjective. 'without' means outside, an old sense crosswords use.
explanation.definitionFit: Bourgeois describes middle-class conventional attitudes, conservative in taste and politics.

clue.text: "Short Conservatives with kit off" is available to buy now

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Cons is the short form of Conservatives
joins the two parts of the fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about Tories stripping off, promoted as a hot buy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kit off' reads as getting undressed, but 'off' is the signal to jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods in stock are held by the shop, so they can be bought immediately.

clue.text: Best thing to do with an Archer novel to get Speaker's support?

blocks.note: the advice is to pulp the book, recycling it into paper mush
the novel is referred to as 'it'

explanation.surface: A jibe at Jeffrey Archer's novels, wondering how a speaker might get backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer is a Conservative peer and bestselling novelist whom Private Eye mocks; 'pulp it' is the scornful verdict on his book.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulpit is the raised stand from which a preacher addresses a congregation, supporting the speaker.

clue.text: Reveal tits, having grasped the source of roué's ejaculation

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter is taken
to grasp is to hold within, so one piece encloses the letter

blocks.note: to out someone is to reveal them
a slang synonym for breasts
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lecherous old roué's reaction to a woman exposing her breasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ejaculation' has an old innocent sense: a sudden exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejaculation in its older sense is a sudden spoken exclamation, which is an outburst.

clue.text: "Bread, man!" a tit snapped

indicators.note: something snapped is broken, so these letters are broken up and reformed

blocks.note: a chap is a man
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A fool snaps 'Bread, man!' as if demanding food or money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tit' is British slang for an idiot as well as a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapatti is an unleavened flatbread from Indian cookery.

clue.text: Jerk-like, dumbo Cameron's lead extremely hairy

indicators.note: the lead is at the front, so the name contributes only its opening letter
at the extremes means the two end letters of the word

blocks.note: a twit is a fool
the opening letter of the name
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An insult describing David Cameron as a hairy idiot of a jerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' wants to be an insult like dumbo; here it is a sudden twitch of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitchy describes someone given to sudden jerky movements, nervous and jumpy.

clue.text: Redneck gay getting some stick?

blocks.note: first meaning: a homophobic slur for a gay man, the sort of word a bigot uses
second meaning: a bundle of sticks tied together for firewood

explanation.surface: A gay man receiving abuse from a bigoted redneck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting some stick' sounds like being harassed, but 'some stick' is the bundled firewood sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an American homophobic slur and also an old term for a bundle of kindling twigs.

clue.text: Dad's about to penetrate duke who has a fetish

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a person

indicators.note: moved about, the letters of the word are shifted into a new order
to penetrate is to go inside, so the jumbled letters enter the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
dukes is slang for fists, as in 'put up your dukes'

explanation.surface: Dad is about to have his way with an aristocrat with peculiar tastes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duke' looks like the nobleman, abbreviated D, but it is slang for a fist.
explanation.definitionFit: A faddist is someone with a craze or fixation, a person devoted to a passing enthusiasm.

clue.text: Wicked in bed, guard, not having been "snipped"?

indicators.note: something wicked is twisted, so the letters that follow are twisted around

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A naughty bodyguard in bed, whose manhood has not been snipped.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes around 'snipped' hint at vasectomy or circumcision; the real sense is a text that has not been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: An unabridged book is complete, with nothing cut out of the text.

clue.text: Squeeze boner dry, if nuts not right

indicators.note: 'not' tells the solver to leave out the next letter from the collection
nuts means mad, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right, here removed once

explanation.surface: Smutty advice on squeezing a bone dry, with nuts in the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeeze' looks like the verb; it is the noun, slang for a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeeze is informal slang for a romantic partner, such as a boyfriend.

clue.text: Boris's version of our strip is OK to be broadcast?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: taken as written, then scattered

explanation.surface: Asking whether Boris Johnson's take on a Private Eye cartoon may be aired.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye ran a cartoon strip called Yobs; posh Boris Johnson would call yobs oiks.
explanation.definitionFit: Oik is upper-class British slang for a coarse, lower-class lout, the toff's word for a yob.

clue.text: see 24dn.
The product of hernial surgery, so no youthful Clinton?

indicators.note: surgery cuts and rearranges, so the letters of the word are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Something produced by a hernia operation, and a dig at Bill Clinton.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Clinton famously said he tried cannabis as a student but 'didn't inhale', so the young Clinton was no inhaler.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler is one who breathes in smoke, which Clinton claimed he never did in his youth.

clue.text: Conservative member initially falling into neglect gets "bonus"

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used
falling into something puts it inside, so the letter enters the longer word

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
an omission is something neglected or left out
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Tory MP who neglects his duties still pockets a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes around 'bonus' hint that the payment is a dubious kickback.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is a percentage payment to an agent, effectively a bonus on sales.

clue.text: Tony in Cherie's eyes, when he ditched traditional Labour principles?

definitions.text: Tony in Cherie's eyes, when he ditched traditional Labour principles?

blocks.note: surface reading: how Cherie Blair saw her husband, the perfect man to marry

blocks.clueFragment: when he ditched traditional Labour principles
blocks.note: setter's reading: Tony Blair moved his party to the political right with New Labour

explanation.surface: Cherie Blair's view of her husband Tony as he abandoned old Labour values.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair, Labour prime minister, steered the party rightwards; his wife Cherie presumably saw him as the ideal husband.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the ideal partner, and here also puns on a man who has moved rightward politically.

clue.text: see 1ac.
Stroppy Hirst's pickled yak's head

indicators.note: pickled means drunk and muddled, so the name's letters are mixed up
the head is the top, so only the opening letter of the animal is taken

blocks.note: the surname, taken as written then jumbled
the opening letter of the animal

explanation.surface: Damien Hirst, the artist known for animals preserved in formaldehyde, pickles a yak's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Hirst's pickled shark and sheep make 'pickled' a natural surface word; here it signals a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirty is British informal for bad-tempered and irritable, a synonym of stroppy.

clue.text: Credit ever crunched, CD released: "Repossess!"

indicators.note: letters released are let go, so they leave the collection
something crunched is crushed out of shape, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A financial headline: the credit crunch is here and bailiffs are told to repossess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Credit crunch' is the 2008 financial crisis; split here, 'crunched' is the jumble signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To repossess is to take back goods, which is to retrieve them.

clue.text: (& 17ac.) Bad guy, lacking capital, goes to financial quarter – not a flourishing area these days?

definitions.text: not a flourishing area these days?

indicators.note: the capital is the opening letter, and lacking it means that letter is dropped

blocks.note: a sinner is a wrongdoer
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A crook, having lost his money, heads to the financial district, no longer booming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' tempts as money or London, but it means a capital letter, the opening S.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner-city districts are associated with deprivation and decline, hardly flourishing areas.

clue.text: see 1ac.
(& 27dn.) Space CIA, rid of boundaries, turned up in an Antarctic area?

indicators.note: with the outer edges stripped away, only the inner run of letters across the two words is kept
in a down entry, turned up means the letters run from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the two words with their outermost letters stripped

explanation.surface: A US spy agency loose in space, turning up over Antarctica.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outer letters from the two words together and read what is left backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent sheet of ice covering polar land, as Antarctica has.

clue.text: Johnny's political party ring escaping ruin

indicators.note: the round letter escapes, so it leaves the word for disaster

blocks.note: Con is short for the Conservative party
O is ring-shaped
doom is ruin, a terrible fate

explanation.surface: A politician called Johnny sees his party escape disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'johnny' (rubber johnny) is British slang for a condom.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnny is British slang for the contraceptive sheath, the rubber johnny.

clue.text: see 26dn.
Rancour of BBC head consumed by perverted urge

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so these letters are rearranged
something consumed is taken inside, so the abbreviation goes within the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the head of the BBC is its Director-General, DG

explanation.surface: A BBC boss brought down by a pervert's urges, with bitterness all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'BBC head' suggests the letter B; the head of the BBC is its Director-General.
explanation.definitionFit: A grudge is lasting resentment or ill will, which is rancour.

clue.text: High-ups shy about pressure underwear

indicators.note: about means around, so the throwing word wraps the other two

blocks.note: to shy is to throw, or toss
P is the symbol for pressure
a bra is an undergarment

explanation.surface: Senior figures turning bashful over pressure about their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like the adjective bashful; it is the verb meaning throw, as at a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: The top brass are the most senior officers or executives, those high up in an organisation.
